question_reframed: How do lineage-specific rates of repeat-DNA gain, whole-genome duplication, and DNA loss jointly generate extreme nuclear genome-size divergence, and when do genome-size-associated phenotypes impose evolutionary constraints?

evidence_cards.claim: Land plants exhibit exceptionally broad genome-size variation with substantial sampling gaps.
Repeat accumulation and TE-family turnover can explain large fractions of within-clade genome-size differences.
Genome reduction can follow WGD and may involve loss of intergenic/repetitive DNA.
Genome size may covary with cellular and life-history traits, but causal generalization is unresolved.

prohibited_inferences: A repeat fraction is a universal causal explanation of genome size.
Whole-genome duplication determines current genome size without modeling subsequent loss.
A genome-size trait correlation establishes adaptation or causal direction.
A literature-backed mechanism is an observed outcome in a new lineage.
